findings.issue_text: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid never consumes recovery codes (only anyMatch, no removal/update), allowing a single recovery code to be replayed indefinitely, unlike the DB-backed RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider

BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential stores raw recovery codes in plaintext, and CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential hands raw codes to any user storage provider, leaking secrets to federated stores instead of hashed codes

RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator/RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean: federated getCredentials rebuilds the credential from the full raw list via createFromValues on every call, so getNextRecoveryAuthnCode() always returns code #0 and the authenticator's remove-used-code logic has no effect on user storage
CredentialHelper.java:117 uses hardcoded string "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes" instead of RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProviderFactory.PROVIDER_ID, risking null provider and NPE on fallback path
CredentialHelper.java:119 passes empty-string credential ID to new UserCredentialModel("", type, json) instead of null, which may cause providers branching on non-null ID to treat it as an update

CredentialHelper.java:122 treats updateCredential returning false as 'not supported' and falls back to local DB, but false is also returned on storage failure, potentially producing duplicate credentials with no distinction between 'not supported' and 'failed'

RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential prefers the federated credential over the local one, so users with both local and user-storage codes are validated against the wrong set with no documented precedence or migration

RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils in server-spi now depends on UserModel.credentialManager() and RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, coupling a generic util to the credential-manager runtime and changing the public SPI surface without @since/deprecation notes

BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials and isValid use unchecked raw List from JsonSerialization.readValue passed to createFromValues(List<String>), so non-string elements cause ClassCastException at runtime rather than the caught IOException

BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials override returns only recovery codes + OTP, dropping the password credential from the federated credential stream and changing behavior seen by account console/admin endpoints for a provider that must remain 4.8.3-compatible

BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage class Javadoc claims future Keycloak versions should not require changing the provider, yet the PR modifies it to add a new credential type; recovery-code support should arguably live in a separate test provider

BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin only asserts a single login with code 0; missing tests for reusing a consumed code, second login asking for code 1, an invalid code, and the local-DB fallback path

BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.configureBrowserFlowWithRecoveryAuthnCodes adds a delayed-authenticator execution whose delay parameter is always 0 (dead), and the config alias is misspelled 'delayed-suthenticator-config', indicating unadapted copy-paste from BrowserFlowTest

BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.setupRecoveryKeysForUserWithRequiredAction and assertUserHasRecoveryKeysCredentialInUserStorage hardcode username "otp1" and ignore the userId argument, so future tests with different users would silently test the wrong account

goldens.comment: Unsafe raw List deserialization without type safety. Calling Optional.get() directly on the Optional returned by RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) without checking isPresent() can lead to a NoSuchElementException if the Optional is empty.

After creating the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, consider setting its id from the stored credential (e.g., myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()); otherwise getId() will be null and downstream removal by id (e.g., removeStoredCredentialById in the authenticator flow) may not work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid never consumes recovery codes (only anyMatch, no removal/update), allowing a single recovery code to be replayed indefinitely, unlike the DB-backed RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds RecoveryAuthnCodes validation to `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid(...)`. In the new branch `else if (input.getType().equals(RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE))`, it deserializes the stored list of recovery codes and returns `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))`. There is no code path that removes the matched code from the stored list (`myUser.recoveryCodes`) or updates the credential after a successful match. As a result, the same recovery code would remain valid and can be replayed indefinitely for this user-storage provider, which is inconsistent with one-time recovery code semantics (and with typical DB-backed implementations that consume codes).

adjudication_records.issue_text: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential stores raw recovery codes in plaintext, and CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential hands raw codes to any user storage provider, leaking secrets to federated stores instead of hashed codes

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows raw recovery codes being serialized and passed into federated user storage via the generic credential update path. In CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential, `generatedCodes` (the plaintext codes shown to the user) are converted to JSON (`JsonSerialization.writeValueAsString(generatedCodes)`) and put into a `UserCredentialModel(..., recoveryCodesJson)`, then `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(recoveryCodesCredential)` is invoked. Any user storage provider that supports this credential type will receive the plaintext codes as the credential input. The testsuite federated provider confirms this behavior: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential for `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE` stores `input.getChallengeResponse()` directly into `recoveryCodesModel.setCredentialData(...)`, and its `isValid` later deserializes that list and compares by equality, meaning the codes are stored and used in plaintext. This is a verifiable secret-handling/security issue introduced by the change for federated storage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator/RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean: federated getCredentials rebuilds the credential from the full raw list via createFromValues on every call, so getNextRecoveryAuthnCode() always returns code #0 and the authenticator's remove-used-code logic has no effect on user storage
CredentialHelper.java:117 uses hardcoded string "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes" instead of RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProviderFactory.PROVIDER_ID, risking null provider and NPE on fallback path

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a hardcoded provider id string in `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential`: `session.getProvider(CredentialProvider.class, "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes")`. However, the finding’s core claim (that this risks a null provider because it should use `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProviderFactory.PROVIDER_ID`) is not verifiable from the diff: we cannot see the constant’s value, so we can’t confirm a mismatch. The potential NPE on the fallback path (`recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(...)`) would only occur if the provider is missing, which is also true even if a constant were used and is not uniquely caused by the hardcoded string in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CredentialHelper.java:119 passes empty-string credential ID to new UserCredentialModel("", type, json) instead of null, which may cause providers branching on non-null ID to treat it as an update

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `new UserCredentialModel("", credentialModel.getType(), recoveryCodesJson)` in `createRecoveryCodesCredential`, i.e., an empty-string ID is passed. However, the proposed impact (“providers branching on non-null ID to treat it as an update”) is not verifiable from the diff: no provider logic or `UserCredentialModel`/`updateCredential` semantics are shown that would treat "" differently from `null` or cause an incorrect update path. This is therefore speculative based solely on the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CredentialHelper.java:122 treats updateCredential returning false as 'not supported' and falls back to local DB, but false is also returned on storage failure, potentially producing duplicate credentials with no distinction between 'not supported' and 'failed'

adjudication.rationale: In the added `createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)` method, the code uses the boolean result of `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)` to decide whether the credential was created in federated user storage (true) or should be created in local storage (false). The diff itself does not show (or imply) that `updateCredential` returns `false` on storage *failure*; in the only user-storage implementation modified here (`BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential`), `false` is returned only for unsupported credential types, while supported paths return `true` (and failures would more plausibly throw). Therefore the finding’s claim that `false` also represents “storage failure” and can lead to duplicates is not verifiable from this diff and is speculative about behavior outside the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential prefers the federated credential over the local one, so users with both local and user-storage codes are validated against the wrong set with no documented precedence or migration

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(UserModel)` which explicitly documents and implements the precedence: it checks federated (user storage) recovery-codes first, and only falls back to local stored credentials if none are found. That precedence is therefore documented in the new Javadoc, and the choice itself isn’t a verifiable defect from the diff alone. The claim that this causes validation against the “wrong set” when both exist is speculative (the diff doesn’t establish that having both is a supported/expected state or that local should win).

adjudication_records.issue_text: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils in server-spi now depends on UserModel.credentialManager() and RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, coupling a generic util to the credential-manager runtime and changing the public SPI surface without @since/deprecation notes

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new public helper method `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(UserModel)` in `server-spi` that imports/uses `UserModel`, `CredentialModel`, and `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` and calls `user.credentialManager()`. This is an intentional API addition to a recovery-codes-specific utility (not a generic util), and it is backward compatible (no existing method signatures changed). The complaint about “coupling” and missing `@since`/deprecation notes is a design/documentation preference rather than a verifiable defect (bug/security/correctness issue) introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials and isValid use unchecked raw List from JsonSerialization.readValue passed to createFromValues(List<String>), so non-string elements cause ClassCastException at runtime rather than the caught IOException

adjudication.rationale: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials(), the code deserializes JSON with `JsonSerialization.readValue(..., List.class)` into a raw `List` and then passes it to `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...)`, which (by its generic intent/signature) expects a `List<String>`. If the stored JSON is malformed or contains non-string elements, Jackson will still produce a `List` (e.g., Integers/Maps) without throwing `IOException`, and downstream processing in `createFromValues` can trigger a `ClassCastException` that is not caught (only `IOException` is caught). The diff clearly introduces this unchecked/raw deserialization pattern. The finding’s mention of `isValid` is weaker because `isValid` only compares via `equals` and may not throw, but the core issue in `getCredentials` is real.

adjudication_records.issue_text: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials override returns only recovery codes + OTP, dropping the password credential from the federated credential stream and changing behavior seen by account console/admin endpoints for a provider that must remain 4.8.3-compatible

BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage class Javadoc claims future Keycloak versions should not require changing the provider, yet the PR modifies it to add a new credential type; recovery-code support should arguably live in a separate test provider

adjudication.rationale: The diff does modify `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage` to support `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE`, which arguably contradicts the Javadoc’s aspirational statement about future versions not needing changes. However, this is not a verifiable bug/security/correctness defect introduced by the code change; it’s a documentation/design preference issue (the comment already contains a TODO and is not a guarantee). The suggestion to move recovery-code support to a separate test provider is also architectural speculation, not a concrete defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin only asserts a single login with code 0; missing tests for reusing a consumed code, second login asking for code 1, an invalid code, and the local-DB fallback path

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new integration test `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` that performs one successful login using recovery code index 0. The proposed finding complains about missing additional scenarios (reuse consumed code, second login, invalid code, DB fallback). Those are test coverage suggestions, not a verifiable defect/bug introduced by the diff. Nothing in the diff indicates the current test is incorrect or that the feature fails without those extra assertions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.configureBrowserFlowWithRecoveryAuthnCodes adds a delayed-authenticator execution whose delay parameter is always 0 (dead), and the config alias is misspelled 'delayed-suthenticator-config', indicating unadapted copy-paste from BrowserFlowTest

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `configureBrowserFlowWithRecoveryAuthnCodes(KeycloakTestingClient testingClient, long delay)` uses the passed `delay` to set `config.setConfig(Map.of("delay", Long.toString(delay)))`. In this diff it is called once with `0`, but that does not make the code path “dead” or a defect—it's simply configuring a 0 delay for this test. The alias string `"delayed-suthenticator-config"` is misspelled, but the alias appears to be an arbitrary identifier and nothing in the diff demonstrates it is referenced elsewhere or must match a specific value. The finding’s “unadapted copy-paste” claim is speculative and not verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.setupRecoveryKeysForUserWithRequiredAction and assertUserHasRecoveryKeysCredentialInUserStorage hardcode username "otp1" and ignore the userId argument, so future tests with different users would silently test the wrong account

adjudication.rationale: In the added method `setupRecoveryKeysForUserWithRequiredAction(String userId, ...)`, the `userId` parameter is used only to fetch/update the user’s required actions via Admin REST (`testRealm().users().get(userId)`), but the actual login that performs the recovery-codes setup is hardcoded as `testAppHelper.startLogin("otp1", "pass");` rather than deriving the username from `userId`/the user representation. This means if the helper is reused with a different user, it would set the required action on one account but authenticate and configure recovery codes on the hardcoded `otp1` account (i.e., silently testing the wrong user). The part of the finding about `assertUserHasRecoveryKeysCredentialInUserStorage` can’t be verified from the shown diff, but the issue in `setupRecoveryKeysForUserWithRequiredAction` is present in the diff.
